experiment: B — deployment-native scorer (trained on serving oracle) vs H2O, live closed loop
setup: SEER sim, mooncake 4096, 24 prompts, measured-DMA; native = logistic on {within_accum, native_cross, recency} trained on Llama serving oracle
verdict: The serving-native scorer beats H2O OFF-policy (+0.04 recall on H2O-logged features) but LOSES ON-policy in the live closed loop (+0.13 worse eps @b0.20), and the loss reproduces under cross-architecture transfer. The off-policy win is an evaluation artifact: scoring a selector on another selector trace overstates it, because the masking feedback loop degrades the native scorer own observed features. H2O remains unbeaten in the closed loop.
second_methodological_finding: KV selectors must be evaluated CLOSED-LOOP (on-policy). Off-policy evaluation on a trace generated by a different (stronger) policy systematically overstates a learned selector. This is a second, distinct caution beyond the offline-vs-deployment gap (capstone A).
why_H2O_is_at_the_ceiling: The served oracle (current top-B_t of masked attention) is best predicted by accumulated attention; adding cross/recency helps off-policy but the closed-loop optimum collapses to accumulation (H2O). Even DAgger-style on-policy retraining would converge to ~H2O.
